browser_hook.reason: Browser screenshots must ask for a `scale` above 0 and at most {scale}, so the image stays small. Retry the same call with `scale` set to {scale} or lower (split a very large or deeply nested batch into smaller calls), or run `web-shot <url>` for a PNG file within the limits and read the path it prints.
comment_guard.deny: Comment guard: {detail}. Add at most one short rationale comment ({max_lines} line(s) at most) for a non-obvious structural placement decision, never narration, history, dates or decision numbers. Rewrite the change with fewer comments, or ask the user to turn the guard off (unset AGENT_SAFEGUARDS_COMMENT_GUARD, or remove the comment-guard file from the agent-safeguards config folder).
comment_guard.after: Comment guard: {detail}. That file changed while the command that just ran was running, and a command's file writes cannot be stopped in advance. Shorten or remove the new comments in that file now: at most {max_lines} line(s) in one block, never narration, history, dates or decision numbers. If the file must keep them, ask the user to turn the guard off (unset AGENT_SAFEGUARDS_COMMENT_GUARD, or remove the comment-guard file from the agent-safeguards config folder).
comment_guard.trimmed: Comment guard: {count} new comment line(s) over the limit were left out of {file}; the code was written exactly as you wrote it. Left out: {lines}. If the file really needs a comment, add it again with at most {max_lines} line(s) in one block (one short rationale for a non-obvious structural decision, never narration, history, dates or decision numbers).
comment_guard.trimmed_after: Comment guard: {count} new comment line(s) over the limit were removed from {file} after the command wrote it; the rest of the file is as the command left it. Removed: {lines}. If the file really needs a comment, add it again with at most {max_lines} line(s) in one block (one short rationale for a non-obvious structural decision, never narration, history, dates or decision numbers).
comment_guard.detail.history: a new comment in {file} reads like narration or history ({marker})
comment_guard.detail.too_long: a new comment line in {file} is longer than {limit} characters
comment_guard.detail.too_many: this change adds {lines} comment lines in {blocks} block(s) to {file}, and the limit is {max_lines} lines in one block
comment_guard.error.input: comment-guard could not read its input and allowed the call.
comment_guard.error.internal: comment-guard hit an internal error and allowed the call.
comment_guard.check.limits: Limits: {lines} comment line(s) per file, {chars} characters per line.
delete_guard.ask: Delete guard asks first: {reason}. Allow it only if you mean to remove the whole project.
delete_guard.cli.usage: usage: delete-guard hook <claude|codex> | check-remote '<command>' | remote-preflight '<command>' | self-test
delete_guard.deny: Delete guard: {reason}. Delete only literal paths inside the current repository or worktree, or a temp folder. Remove a worktree with `git worktree remove <path>`; move anything else to the Trash with `trash <path>` (`trash-put <path>` or `gio trash <path>` on Linux). Emptying a Trash, or deleting inside one, is for the user to do. Resolve variables and globs first and pass the literal path. If this deletion is really needed, ask the user.
delete_guard.deny_input: Delete guard could not read this command and blocked it. Ask the user to run it outside the agent.
delete_guard.deny_internal: Delete guard hit an internal error while checking this command and blocked it. Ask the user to run it outside the agent.
delete_guard.deny_permission: Delete guard: {reason}. This needs the user's permission and this host cannot ask: tell the user what you want to remove and why, and let them decide.
delete_guard.deny_remote: Delete guard: {reason}. On a remote machine delete only a literal path written as ~/... or /... strictly inside {roots}, with no .., variable, glob, brace or substitution; resolve the name first and pass the literal path. Any other file can go to the Trash with `trash-put <path>` or `gio trash <path>` and a literal path that is not the home folder, a folder directly in it or a system folder, and emptying a Trash is for the user to do. If a deletion elsewhere is really needed, ask the user.
delete_guard.deny_too_slow: Delete guard could not finish checking this command in time and blocked it. Split it into smaller commands, or ask the user to run it outside the agent.
delete_guard.reason.bare_glob: `{verb}` with a bare glob ({raw}) depends on the current folder
delete_guard.reason.computed_path: `{verb}` with a computed path ({raw}) can expand to the wrong folder
delete_guard.reason.device_redirect: a redirection onto the device {path} overwrites it
delete_guard.reason.diskutil: `diskutil` erase and delete operations are irreversible
delete_guard.reason.expansion: `{verb}` target {raw} expands to more names than the guard can check, or through a folder it cannot list
delete_guard.reason.find_follow: `find` with `{option}` follows links, so what it deletes can lie outside the folder it was given
delete_guard.reason.find_roots: `find` takes its starting folders from a file, which the guard cannot check
delete_guard.reason.git_clean: `git clean` deletes untracked files (and with -x every ignored file, such as local notes); run it with -n and remove the listed paths one by one
delete_guard.reason.glob_midpath: `{verb}` with a glob before the last path component ({raw}) can reach folders outside the checked area
delete_guard.reason.in_script: {script} is a script that is not a reviewed file of a repository, and it contains: {reason}
delete_guard.reason.inline_delete: inline code that deletes folders recursively cannot be checked
delete_guard.reason.location: `{verb}` target {raw} is a location the guard cannot check; give a path
delete_guard.reason.match_path: `{verb}` target {raw} is built from a name that find or xargs supplies, which the guard cannot check
delete_guard.reason.outside_repository: `{verb}` target {path} is outside the current repository and temp folders
delete_guard.reason.remote_target: `{verb}` target {raw} on a remote machine is not a literal path strictly inside an allowed folder
delete_guard.reason.remote_trash: `trash` target {raw} on a remote machine is not a literal path, or it is the home folder, a folder directly in it or a system folder
delete_guard.reason.rsync_remote: `rsync` deleting on a remote host:path cannot be checked here
delete_guard.reason.too_large: a delete command that is too large to check
delete_guard.reason.trash_computed: `trash` target {raw} is computed by a command, so the guard cannot tell what it will send to the Trash
delete_guard.reason.trash_empty: `{name}` empties a Trash, or deletes past it, for good
delete_guard.reason.trash_holder: `{verb}` would delete a folder that holds a Trash ({path})
delete_guard.reason.trash_inside: `trash` would move a Trash, or a folder that holds one, into the Trash ({path})
delete_guard.reason.trash_purge: `{verb}` would delete from a Trash ({path}), which holds files the user can still restore
delete_guard.reason.trash_repository: `{verb}` would send a whole Git repository, a worktree or a folder that holds repositories to the Trash ({path})
delete_guard.reason.unparseable: a delete command whose quoting cannot be parsed
delete_guard.reason.unresolvable: `{verb}` target {raw} cannot be resolved because the current folder is unknown
delete_guard.reason.worktree: {path} is a Git worktree or submodule; use `git worktree remove {path}`
delete_guard.reason.xargs_option: an `xargs` option that cannot be read, so the command it runs is not known
delete_guard.reason.xargs_rm: `xargs rm` deletes paths the guard cannot see
safe_tool.ask.local_artifact: Tracking a machine-local agent artifact requires explicit user approval.
safe_tool.cli.usage: usage: safe-tool hook <claude|codex> | self-test | status coderabbit | status rtk | has-key <NAME> [<NAME> ...] [--file <startup file>] | remote-readonly '<command>' | redact | git identity | git commit -m <message> [-m <message> ...]
safe_tool.deny.git_format: Sensitive-output command blocked: this git command can print author or committer names, emails or message bodies (the default log format, or a format with %an, %ae, %cn, %ce, %b, %B and the like). Use `--oneline`, or `--format` with only hashes, subjects, ref names and dates, for example `git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short`; for `git for-each-ref` use fields such as `%(refname:short) %(committerdate:short)`. `safe-tool git identity` says whether an identity is set.
safe_tool.deny.internal: agent-safeguards hit an internal error while checking this command and blocked it. Ask the user to run it outside the agent.
safe_tool.deny.key_file: Read blocked: those lines hold a key. Agents may write keys into files for the user but never read them. Read a range that leaves the key out, find the lines you need with `rg -l` or `rg -c`, or ask the user.
safe_tool.deny.proxy: `rtk proxy` is limited to a short list of text tools (awk, cat, cmp, diff, du, find, git, grep, head, ls, nl, rg, sed, sort, stat, tail, uniq, wc). Run the command without `rtk proxy`, or as `rtk <tool>`.
safe_tool.deny.rtk: RTK is required for this supported shell command. Rerun it through rtk.
safe_tool.deny.sensitive: Sensitive-output command blocked. Use safe-tool or ask the user to run it outside the agent.
safe_tool.deny.startup_file: Shell startup and history files can hold secrets, so they are not read. Reload one with `source <file>`, or check whether a key is set with `safe-tool has-key <NAME>`, which prints NAME=pass, NAME=fail or NAME=unknown and never the value.
safe_tool.deny.too_slow: agent-safeguards could not finish checking this command in time and blocked it. Split it into smaller commands, or ask the user to run it outside the agent.
safe_tool.remote.reason.command: `{name}` is not on the read list
safe_tool.remote.reason.operand: `{name}` with an operand that sets the clock or names a file it would write
safe_tool.remote.reason.option: `{name}` with `{option}` can change the machine or never end
safe_tool.remote.reason.sensitive: it asks for credentials, the environment, a startup file or a secret path
safe_tool.remote.reason.shape: it is not one pipeline of simple commands (no redirect, ; && || &, substitution, line break or an unclosed quote)
safe_tool.remote.reason.subcommand: `{name} {subcommand}` is not on the read list
safe_tool.remote.refused: Remote command refused: {reason}. The machine is reached read-only: one pipeline of read commands ({commands}), filtered on the machine so only what the task needs comes back. If a change is really needed, ask the user to run it.
safe_tool.withheld.context: The output of that command was withheld because it holds {why}. Narrow the read (`rg -l`, `rg -c`, `sed -n` on a few lines, leave out the matching line) and retry; ask the user only if the content itself is needed.
safe_tool.withheld.reason: Sensitive command output was withheld. Use safe-tool or ask the user to run the command outside the agent.
safe_tool.withheld.reason_why: Sensitive command output was withheld because it holds {why}. Narrow the read (`rg -l`, `rg -c`, `sed -n` on a few lines, leave out the matching line) and retry; use safe-tool, or ask the user to run the command outside the agent, only if the content itself is needed.
safe_tool.withheld.why.definition: an alias or shell function definition
safe_tool.withheld.why.secret: a value that looks like a key, token or password
screenshot.error.exists: refusing to overwrite an existing file: {path}
screenshot.error.no_sips: sips is needed to shrink this capture, and it is not available
screenshot.error.not_a_png: the capture is not a PNG file
screenshot.error.not_png: the output path must end in .png
screenshot.error.shrink: sips could not shrink the capture
screenshot.error.too_big: the capture could not be kept within {pixels} pixels and {kilobytes} KB, so it was removed
sim_shot.error.no_tools: xcrun is needed, so this runs on macOS with the Xcode command line tools
sim_shot.error.timeout: simctl did not answer in {seconds} seconds. {hint}
sim_shot.hint: Run `xcrun simctl list devices booted` to see what is running. If the capture is refused, skip the screenshot.
simulator_hook.reason: The simulator control tool's screenshot returns an image the API rejects, and one such image breaks this chat for good. Approve only if you, the user, want to run it anyway. Agents: do not retry. Run `sim-shot` (optionally with a new .png path in a temp or scratchpad folder), then read the path it prints with the image reader. If sim-shot fails, skip the screenshot.
web_shot.error.bad_url: only http and https addresses with a plain host name or address, and without a username or password, are allowed
web_shot.error.capture: the browser did not produce a screenshot
web_shot.error.link_local: link-local addresses and the known cloud metadata hosts and addresses are refused
web_shot.error.no_browser: no Chrome, Chromium, Edge or Brave was found to take the screenshot
web_shot.error.timeout: the browser did not finish within {seconds} seconds
